segments.text: Panama Canal reopens after a day-long closure. North Sea wind farm starts supplying power to 1.2 million homes. Lisbon opens a new riverside tram line. Good evening, and welcome to WORLD NOW. I'm Paco Pixel, with Lola Byte.
Breaking news. Ledger Line reports that the Panama Canal has reopened to ships after fog closed it for a day. The canal authority says about 30 ships are waiting to cross.
segments.headline: Panama Canal reopens after a day-long closure

segments.text: Thanks, Paco. From Ledger Line: An offshore wind farm in the North Sea has started supplying electricity. The developer says its 140 turbines can power about 1.2 million homes.
segments.headline: North Sea wind farm starts supplying power to 1.2 million homes

segments.text: Our number of the day: 40,000. Lisbon has opened a new tram line along the Tagus river, Pixelburg Post reports. The city says the 9 kilometre route will carry 40,000 passengers a day and cut car traffic in the old town. As the mayor put it: “This line will change how people move around the old town.”
segments.headline: Lisbon opens a new riverside tram line

quote.text: This line will change how people move around the old town

segments.text: Now, around the world in 30 seconds. Heavy monsoon rain has flooded streets in several coastal towns in Kerala, India, Pixelburg Post reports.
segments.headline: Heavy rain floods streets in coastal towns of Kerala

segments.text: A fissure eruption has started again on the Reykjanes peninsula in Iceland.
segments.headline: Iceland volcano erupts again on the Reykjanes peninsula

segments.text: Venice has raised its sea barriers for a test ahead of the autumn high tides, Bitport Herald reports.
segments.headline: Venice raises its sea barriers in a test before the autumn tides

segments.text: A large solar plant on the edge of the Sahara in Morocco is now running at full power, Bitport Herald reports.
segments.headline: Morocco desert solar plant reaches full power

segments.text: And finally: Scientists say coral cover has grown on parts of the Great Barrier Reef for a second year. “The reef is showing it can bounce back when it gets a break,” a lead researcher said.
segments.headline: Coral recovers on parts of the Great Barrier Reef

quote.text: The reef is showing it can bounce back when it gets a break

segments.text: A good note to end on.
Rare enough that we should enjoy it.
That's WORLD NOW. From Lola Byte and from me, thank you for watching. Stay with us on GLOBIT 24.
